compiled_state.title: [closure-checks-classifier-pass.sh]: long batch dispatches in Bash-tool background -> SIGKILL at ~75min ceiling truncates mid-run (add per-batch safety cap)
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** 18590b9af0 (post-mktemp fix, on main)
* **affected scripts:** plugins/dso/scripts/closure-checks-classifier-pass.sh, plugins/dso/scripts/migrate-closure-checks.sh (--classify mode), and any helper that wraps them in a batch loop

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior (filed at end-of-session 2026-05-22 per user direction; observed during Phase 4 bulk migration session 2026-05-21/22)

#### Expected Behavior

Bulk-classifier batch loops should either complete within bounded wall-time, OR refuse to start when the batch size would predictably exceed the ~75-minute Bash-tool background ceiling. An operator running a one-shot migration session should not lose mid-batch progress to silent SIGKILL.

#### Actual Behavior

Batch 5 of the Phase 4 migration session 2026-05-21/22 dispatched 40 epics in a single background invocation. Per-epic wall-time was dominated by Anthropic API latency (~30-90s/epic). Wall-time accumulated to ~75 minutes before the Bash-tool background process was SIGKILL'd by the harness's effective ceiling. 18 of 40 epics had completed plan-mode (audits via early-exit OR plan files); the remaining 22 were lost.

Cascading effect: the SIGKILL also bypassed the EXIT trap that cleans up mktemp leak files (bug 724a-53f1, now fixed), which left subsequent invocations broken until a manual `rm` workaround was applied.

Per-batch budgets exist (REMAINING_BUDGET=25 ack-items), but those gate USER-ACK items only — not epic count, not wall-time. A 40-epic batch with very few needs-ack items (typical when r=4 auto-approve policy is active) passes the ack-budget gate but still hits the wall-time ceiling.

### 3. Action History

1. 2026-05-21 batch 4: 30-epic background batch completed in ~80 min (close to ceiling but survived).
2. 2026-05-21 batch 5: 40-epic background batch SIGKILL'd at 18/40 (~75 min wall-time).
3. Manual recovery: re-run plan-mode in smaller chunks; apply mktemp cleanup workaround between iterations.
4. Bug 724a-53f1 (mktemp) fixed and merged 2026-05-22, unblocking parallel background batches as a secondary mitigation.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* **Affected**: bulk-migration workflows that dispatch the classifier helper in a loop
* **Related**: bug 724a-53f1 (closed) — mktemp EXIT-trap leak amplified the impact of mid-batch SIGKILL

#### Suggested fix

Add a per-batch SAFETY CAP to the classifier helper (or its bulk wrapper). Two options:

1. **Hard cap with override**: refuse `--plan-output` batch invocations above N epics per process unless `DSO_CLASSIFIER_LONG_BATCH=1` is set. N=~25 is conservative given observed per-epic latency.

2. **Chunked dispatch mode**: have the bulk wrapper split arbitrary epic lists into chunks of ~15 epics, dispatching each chunk as a separate process. Each chunk has its own EXIT trap, so mid-chunk SIGKILL only loses the current chunk, not the whole batch.

Option 2 is more robust; option 1 is faster to ship. They compose: ship option 1 first as a guard rail; layer option 2 as the chunked dispatch wrapper later.

Additional small improvement: emit a one-line warning when REMAINING_BUDGET > 25 AND the loop body has dispatched >15 epics — operator-facing signal that the run is approaching the ceiling and should be checkpointed.

fix-bug:investigation: INVESTIGATION_COMPLETE

## Root Cause (Verified)

The triage classification is accurate. Two scripts are implicated:

### 1. migrate-closure-checks.sh (the batch orchestrator)

- **** (line 85) — this is a cross-session ACK-item budget, not an epic count cap. It counts user-acknowledgment items, not epics processed.
- **** (line 563) — controls structural migration pass batching; has nothing to do with the classifier wall-time.
- When  mode runs on N brainstorm:complete-tagged epics, the outer ticket loop (lines 574–766) iterates ALL N epics in a single Bash process. The only break-out from this loop is when  (line 722), which only triggers when ≥25 items needed user ACK. With the  auto-approve policy active, almost no items need ACK, so the 25-item ACK budget is never consumed and the loop runs for all N epics.
- **No wall-time guard exists anywhere in the file.**  is never referenced.
- **No epic-count cap exists.** There is no  flag, no  config key, no hard check.

### 2. closure-checks-classifier-pass.sh (the per-epic helper)

- Also has no wall-time guard.
- The Anthropic API call uses a 60s per-request  (line 463) but that only bounds a single haiku dispatch, not total invocation time for a multi-item epic.
- Each epic invocation can take 30–90s depending on item count and API latency.
- At 40 epics × ~100s average = ~4000s (~67 min), exceeding the ~75-min Bash-tool background ceiling (4500s).

### Gap Summary

The REMAINING_BUDGET ack-cap (DD5) was designed to limit interactive user-attention load, not total processing time. With auto-approve active, it never fires as a wall-time proxy. There is no second-level guard protecting against SIGKILL on large batches.

## Fix Plan

**Candidate fix — add two guards to migrate-closure-checks.sh:**

1. **Epic-count cap** (, default 20 or config key ): Before the main batch loop in  mode, if , emit a clear message and truncate the list (with a re-run instruction). This prevents accidentally dispatching oversized batches.

2. **Wall-time guard** using bash : Record  at batch start. Inside the per-epic loop, check  (default 3600s = 60 min, leaving a ~15-min buffer before the ~75-min ceiling). On breach, emit a WALL_TIME_EXCEEDED checkpoint message and  out of both loops — allowing the outer summary and progress-file to be written cleanly.

Both guards should be configurable via environment variables (, ) with safe defaults, and documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md.

No changes needed to closure-checks-classifier-pass.sh — the helper is invoked per-epic and is not the accumulator.

## Evidence Quality

- OBSERVED: Ticket description confirms 40-epic batch hit SIGKILL at ~75 min (2026-05-21 session).
- OBSERVED: Neither script contains any , , , , , or  patterns (grep confirmed).
- DOCUMENTED:  guards ACK-item load only; grep confirms the check is  vs , counting  lines from the helper.
- DOCUMENTED:  is for the structural migration pass, not --classify.

## Classification

- **Bug type:** Behavioral — missing safety guard in shell batch loop
- **Complexity confirmed:** TRIVIAL — single file change (migrate-closure-checks.sh), no cross-system dependencies, deterministic fix
- **Manual approval needed:** No — adding a configurable safety cap with a clean exit message is low blast-radius
- **FIXABLE:** Yes

comments.body: fix-bug:investigation: INVESTIGATION_COMPLETE. Root cause verified: migrate-closure-checks.sh has no epic-count cap or wall-time guard. The 25-item CLASSIFIER_BUDGET only caps ACK items (not epics), so with r=4 auto-approve active, the budget never exhausts and all N epics run in one Bash process to SIGKILL. closure-checks-classifier-pass.sh also has no wall-time guard. Fix: add --max-epics cap (default 20, env DSO_CLASSIFY_MAX_EPICS) and SECONDS-based wall-time guard (default 3600s, env DSO_CLASSIFY_WALL_TIME_SECS) to migrate-closure-checks.sh only.
